title: Isaiah 5 — The Song of the Vineyard and the six woes

citations: JPS 1917 Isa 5:1 'a song of my beloved touching his vineyard'
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: cohortative ʾāšîrāh nāʾ, lîḏîḏî 'for my beloved', šîraṯ dôḏî lᵉḵarmô; bᵉqeren ben-šāmen idiom. The ASV/JPS 1917 construal is the standard one and the NRSV 'love-song' alternative is reported; no lens.
wayᵉʿazzᵉqēhû (hapax 'dig over'), wayᵉsaqqᵉlēhû 'clear of stones', śōrēq 'choice vines', yeqeḇ 'winepress/vat', bᵉʾušîm 'wild grapes' with the bʾš 'stink' root noted: all standard.
yôšēḇ yᵉrûšālaim wᵉʾîš yᵉhûḏāh (collective singulars) rendered plural as in ASV; šiṯpû-nāʾ 'judge, please'. Unmarked shift to the owner's first person correctly left unmarked.
mah-laʿăśôṯ ʿôḏ lᵉḵarmî wᵉlōʾ ʿāśîṯî bô; maddûaʿ qiwwêṯî ... wayyaʿaś bᵉʾušîm: exact.

Infinitive absolutes hāsēr / pārōṣ as finite futures; wᵉhāyāh lᵉḇāʿēr parallel to lᵉmirmās supports the grazing homonym, and 'eaten up' is the ASV/JPS 1917 reading. The deliberate split from 6:13 'for burning' is documented in commentary and glossary; no lens.
bāṯāh 'a waste', lōʾ yizzāmēr wᵉlōʾ yēʿāḏēr 'not pruned nor hoed', šāmîr wāšayiṯ 'briers and thorns', mēhamṭîr ... māṭār 'that they rain no rain': standard.

citations: BDB s.v. miśpāḥ ('outpouring [of blood], bloodshed', cf. Arab. safaḥa)
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed (ASV 'oppression'). miśpāḥ is a hapax; 'bloodshed' has the BDB etymological basis and NRSV support, whereas 'oppression'/'violence' are contextual guesses, so the inferred claim is honest. Plain meanings in the line with the paronomasia explained in commentary is the right presentation; 'an outcry' for ṣᵉʿāqāh is the central entry's value and fits Gen 4:10 / 18:20. No lens: the choice is philological.
hôy maggîʿê ḇayiṯ bᵉḇayiṯ ... wᵉhûšaḇtem lᵉḇaddᵉḵem (Hophal 'you are made to dwell'): exact; ʾereṣ territorial 'land' is correct.

citations: NRSV Isa 5:9 'has sworn in my hearing'
verdicts.reasoning: Verbless bᵉʾoznāy YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ with ASV's supplied 'says'; the oath reading (ʾim-lōʾ) is reported in commentary. 'Surely ... without inhabitant' exact.
ʿăśereṯ ṣimdê-ḵerem 'ten acres (yokes)', baṯ ʾeḥāṯ, zeraʿ ḥōmer yaʿăśeh ʾêp̄āh: exact; the commentary's measures note is correct.
maškîmê ḇabbōqer šēḵār yirdōp̄û, mᵉʾaḥărê ḇannešep̄ yayin yaḏlîqēm: 'until wine inflames them' follows ASV's resultative reading of the asyndetic clause; standard.
kinnôr wānēḇel tōp̄ wᵉḥālîl wāyayin mištêhem; pōʿal YHWH lōʾ yabbîṭû, maʿăśēh yāḏāyw lōʾ rāʾû: exact.

gālāh ʿammî (perfect) 'have gone into exile'; MT mᵉṯê 'men of' kept per the MT policy; kāḇôḏ as social nobility correctly kept off the divine-glory entry. Minor optional style point: English mixes 'my people have' with 'its honored men ... its multitude' (Hebrew 3ms suffix on collective ʿam); ASV/JPS 1917 'their' would read more smoothly, but the current line is not wrong.

citations: H. W. Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament (1974), ch. 2 (nepeš as throat; Isa 5:14, Hab 2:5)
JPS 1917 Isa 5:14 (verified): 'And down goeth their glory, and their tumult, and their uproar, And he that rejoiceth among them'
NRSV Isa 5:14 'the nobility of Jerusalem and her multitude go down, her throng and all who exult in her'
verdicts.reasoning: The line is approved: nap̄šāh 'its throat' parallel to pîhā is lexicon-attested, and keeping the feminine suffixes as 'her' is accurate. REVISE commentary only: the note says the translation 'keeps her with JPS 1917', but JPS 1917 has 'their glory ... among them', like ASV. Replace 'with JPS 1917' by 'with NRSV, which names the referent ("the nobility of Jerusalem and her multitude ... all who exult in her")', and say that ASV and JPS 1917 both smooth to 'their'.

citations: JPS 1917 Isa 5:15 'And man is bowed down, And man is humbled' (verified)
NRSV Isa 5:15 'People are bowed down, everyone is brought low'
ASV 'the mean man ... the great man'
BDB s.v. ʾîš (generic 'each, anyone' in parallel with ʾāḏām)
Ps 49:3 bᵉnê ʾāḏām gam-bᵉnê ʾîš (the social merism ASV reads in)
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: wayyiššaḥ ʾāḏām wayyišpal-ʾîš, two near-synonyms for 'human being'; the Editor is right that ASV's social merism is not marked in the text (it needs the Ps 49:3 pattern, which is absent here). The problem with 'humankind ... man' is register, not accuracy: it puts a gender-neutral collective next to a gender-marked singular for two synonyms. Defensible options: (A) keep 'humankind ... man' (wave ruling, consistent with 2:9, 11, 17 as drafted); (C1) 'humankind is bowed down, and everyone is brought low' (NRSV-type, neutral, keeps ʾāḏām's collective sense); (C2) 'people are bowed down, and each one brought low'. The reviewer leans to C1 for this line and 2:9 ('So humankind is bowed down, and everyone is brought low'); 2:11 and 2:17 'the loftiness of men' would then become 'the loftiness of all people' or 'human loftiness'. This is a project-wide gender-language stance across four verses in two chapters, so it needs one human ruling.

wayyiḡbah YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ bammišpāṭ, hāʾēl haqqāḏôš niqdaš biṣḏāqāh. 'But' for the waw is an acceptable contrast with v 15; appositional 'God the Holy One' (ASV) is kept with the attributive option noted. Split mišpāṭ/ṣᵉḏāqāh correctly kept off the conjoined-pair entry.

citations: NRSV 'fatlings and kids shall feed among the ruins'
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed against NRSV. wᵉrāʿû kᵉḇāśîm kᵉḏāḇrām; MT gārîm 'sojourners' (ASV/JPS 1917 'wanderers') kept per the MT policy, with LXX and the conjectures reported. Defensible and source-honest.
mōšᵉḵê heʿāwōn bᵉḥaḇlê haššāwᵉʾ, wᵉḵaʿăḇôṯ hāʿăḡālāh ḥaṭṭāʾāh: 'cords of falsehood ... cart ropes' as ASV; ʿāwōn 'iniquity' per the central entry.
yᵉmahēr yāḥîšāh maʿăśēhû lᵉmaʿan nirʾeh; wᵉṯiqraḇ wᵉṯāḇôʾāh ʿăṣaṯ qᵉḏôš yiśrāʾēl wᵉnēḏāʿāh: exact; quotation marks are justified by hāʾōmᵉrîm.
Three antithetical pairs (raʿ/ṭôḇ, ḥōšeḵ/ʾôr, mar/māṯôq) with śāmîm ... lᵉ- 'put ... for': exact.
ḥăḵāmîm bᵉʿênêhem wᵉneḡeḏ pᵉnêhem nᵉḇōnîm: 'in their own eyes ... in their own sight' standard.
gibbôrîm lištôṯ yāyin wᵉʾanšê-ḥayil limsōḵ šēḵār: 'mighty at drinking wine, valiant men at mixing strong drink' keeps the irony of the military terms; ʾanšê here is literal plural 'men'.
maṣdîqê rāšāʿ ʿēqeḇ šōḥaḏ; ṣiḏqaṯ ṣaddîqîm yāsîrû mimmennû: the singular 'from him' after plural ṣaddîqîm is kept as in ASV (distributive); exact.

citations: Jensen, The Use of tôrâ by Isaiah (CBQMS 3, 1973)
verdicts.reasoning: kᵉʾĕḵōl qaš lᵉšôn ʾēš waḥăšaš lehāḇāh yirpeh; šoršām kammāq ... pirḥām kāʾāḇāq: exact. tôrāh 'teaching' parallel to ʾimrāh follows the inferred overlay entry and 1:10; defensible.

citations: JPS 1917 'For all this His anger is not turned away, But His hand is stretched out still' (verified)
verdicts.reasoning: ḥārāh ʾap-YHWH ... wayyēṭ yāḏô ʿālāyw wayyakkēhû ... kassûḥāh 'like refuse'. The refrain wording 'For all this his anger has not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still' is idiomatic, matches the perfect lōʾ-šāḇ, and is fit to be fixed for Heb. 9:11, 16, 20; 10:4. 'and' for wᵉ is literal and loses nothing; ASV 'but' remains a legitimate alternative, not a correction.

citations: NRSV 'a nation far away' (emending to lᵉḡôy mimmerḥāq)
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed against NRSV. MT laggôyim mērāḥôq kept with the singular lô / yāḇôʾ rendered collectively, as ASV and JPS 1917 ('unto them ... they shall come'); the emendation is reported. Source-honest.
ʾên-ʿāyēp̄ wᵉʾên-kôšēl bô ... ʾēzôr ḥălāṣāyw ... śᵉrôḵ nᵉʿālāyw: exact, with collective 'them/their'.
ḥiṣṣāyw šᵉnûnîm, qaššᵉṯōṯāyw dᵉruḵôṯ 'bent' (trodden = strung), parsôṯ sûsāyw kaṣṣar 'as flint', galgillāyw kassûp̄āh: standard.

wᵉyinhōm ʿālāyw ... kᵉnahămaṯ-yām; wᵉnibbaṭ lāʾāreṣ. The accents (zaqef on ḥōšeḵ and wāʾôr) are reported correctly in commentary and ASV's grouping is a legitimate departure; ʿărîp̄eyhā hapax 'its clouds'.

paragraphs.text: אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙ לִֽידִידִ֔י שִׁירַ֥ת דּוֹדִ֖י לְכַרְמ֑וֹ כֶּ֛רֶם הָיָ֥ה לִֽידִידִ֖י בְּקֶ֥רֶן בֶּן־שָֽׁמֶן׃

i18n.en: Let me sing for my beloved a song of my beloved concerning his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fruitful hill.

notes.official:
*šîraṯ dôḏî* — the prophet sings *lîḏîḏî* “for my beloved” a song *of* (or *about*) his beloved, and the friend's vineyard. The translation keeps ASV's “a song of my beloved concerning his vineyard”; NRSV's “my love-song” reads *dôḏî* as “my love,” often by emending to *dôḏîm*, and is not adopted. The love-song genre is the bait: the poem opens as a wedding-feast song and turns, at v 3, into a lawsuit in which the owner speaks for himself and the hearers are made judges of their own case — the juridical-parable form of Nathan's ewe-lamb story (2 Sam 12:1–7; Yee, *CBQ* 43 [1981] 30–40; Wildberger, *Isaiah 1–12*, 1991; Williamson, ICC *Isaiah 1–5*, 2006).

*bᵉqeren ben-šāmen* is literally “on a horn, a son of oil”: a hilltop (“horn”) of rich soil (“son of oil” = fat, fertile). The line gives the sense with ASV, “on a very fruitful hill.”

paragraphs.translit: ʾāšīrāh nāʾ līdīdī šīrat dōdī ləkarmō kerem hāyāh līdīdī bəqeren ben-šāmen

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְעַזְּקֵ֣הוּ וַֽיְסַקְּלֵ֗הוּ וַיִּטָּעֵ֙הוּ֙ שֹׂרֵ֔ק וַיִּ֤בֶן מִגְדָּל֙ בְּתוֹכ֔וֹ וְגַם־יֶ֖קֶב חָצֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ וַיְקַ֛ו לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עֲנָבִ֖ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בְּאֻשִֽׁים׃

i18n.en: He dug it and cleared it of stones, and planted it with choice vines; he built a tower in the midst of it, and also hewed out a winepress in it; and he waited for it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes.

notes.official: *bᵉʾušîm* (also v 4), from *bʾš* “to stink,” names the bad fruit. BDB glosses “stinking or worthless things, wild grapes”; the translation keeps the standard “wild grapes” (ASV, JPS 1917, NRSV), and the root's sense of rotten, foul-smelling fruit is noted here.

paragraphs.translit: wayʿazzəqēhū waysaqqəlēhū wayyiṭṭāʿēhū śōrēq wayyiben migdāl bətōkō wəgam-yeqeb ḥāṣēb bō wayqaw laʿăśōt ʿănābīm wayyaʿaś bəʾušīm

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֛ה יוֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֑ה שִׁפְטוּ־נָ֕א בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין כַּרְמִֽי׃

i18n.en: And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge, please, between me and my vineyard.

notes.official: From this verse the owner speaks in the first person (“between me and my vineyard”) without any marked change of speaker; v 7 then names him as YHWH of hosts. The translation adds no quotation marks for vv 3–6, keeping the unmarked shift the Hebrew uses (as ASV).

paragraphs.translit: wəʿattāh yōšēb yərūšālim wəʾīš yəhūdāh šipṭū-nāʾ bēnī ūbēn karmī

paragraphs.text: מַה־לַּעֲשׂ֥וֹת עוֹד֙ לְכַרְמִ֔י וְלֹ֥א עָשִׂ֖יתִי בּ֑וֹ מַדּ֧וּעַ קִוֵּ֛יתִי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עֲנָבִ֖ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בְּאֻשִֽׁים׃

i18n.en: What more was there to do for my vineyard that I have not done in it? Why, when I waited for it to yield grapes, did it yield wild grapes?

paragraphs.translit: mah-laʿăśōt ʿōd ləkarmī wəlōʾ ʿāśītī bō maddūaʿ qiwwētī laʿăśōt ʿănābīm wayyaʿaś bəʾušīm

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּה֙ אוֹדִֽיעָה־נָּ֣א אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֖ה לְכַרְמִ֑י הָסֵ֤ר מְשׂוּכָּתוֹ֙ וְהָיָ֣ה לְבָעֵ֔ר פָּרֹ֥ץ גְּדֵר֖וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְמִרְמָֽס׃

i18n.en: And now let me tell you what I am about to do to my vineyard: I will remove its hedge, and it shall be eaten up; I will break down its wall, and it shall be trampled down.

notes.official: *wᵉhāyāh lᵉḇāʿēr* is the same infinitive the translation renders “for burning” at 6:13. Here it is paired with *lᵉmirmās* “for trampling” after the hedge is removed, and the line reads the homonym *bʿr* II “graze, browse” (cf. Exod 22:4), hence ASV's “it shall be eaten up” (NRSV “devoured”). The 6:13 decision (`levaer-massevet-stump-isaiah`, *bʿr* I “burn”) does not govern this site; the separate overlay entry `baar-graze-vineyard-isaiah-5` records the split.

paragraphs.translit: wəʿattāh ʾōdīʿāh-nāʾ ʾetkem ʾēt ʾăšer-ʾănī ʿōśeh ləkarmī hāsēr məśūkkātō wəhāyāh ləbāʿēr pārōṣ gədērō wəhāyāh ləmirmās

paragraphs.text: וַאֲשִׁיתֵ֣הוּ בָתָ֗ה לֹ֤א יִזָּמֵר֙ וְלֹ֣א יֵעָדֵ֔ר וְעָלָ֥ה שָׁמִ֖יר וָשָׁ֑יִת וְעַ֤ל הֶעָבִים֙ אֲצַוֶּ֔ה מֵהַמְטִ֥יר עָלָ֖יו מָטָֽר׃

i18n.en: And I will make it a waste; it shall not be pruned nor hoed, and briers and thorns shall come up; and I will command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.

paragraphs.translit: waʾăšītēhū bātāh lōʾ yizzāmēr wəlōʾ yēʿādēr wəʿālāh šāmīr wāšāyit wəʿal heʿābīm ʾăṣawweh mēhamṭīr ʿālāyw māṭār

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י כֶ֜רֶם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה נְטַ֖ע שַׁעֲשׁוּעָ֑יו וַיְקַ֤ו לְמִשְׁפָּט֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשְׂפָּ֔ח לִצְדָקָ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה צְעָקָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For the vineyard of YHWH of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the planting of his delight; and he waited for justice, but behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, but behold, an outcry.

notes.official:
The song ends in a double pun: *wayqaw lᵉmišpāṭ wᵉhinnēh miśpāḥ, liṣḏāqāh wᵉhinnēh ṣᵉʿāqāh* — “he waited for *mišpāṭ* (justice), and behold *miśpāḥ*; for *ṣᵉḏāqāh* (righteousness), and behold *ṣᵉʿāqāh*.” Each pair differs by a single consonant. English cannot reproduce it without bending the sense: NJPS's echo “justice … injustice; equity … iniquity” keeps the sound but turns the cry of victims into an abstract wrong. The translation keeps the meanings in the line and states the pun here.

*miśpāḥ* is a hapax. Derived from a root “pour out” (of blood; cf. Arabic *safaḥa*), it gives “bloodshed” (BDB; NRSV), the reading adopted here; ASV's “oppression” and JPS 1917's “violence” are context guesses. “Bloodshed” also sits with the hands “full of blood” of 1:15.

*ṣᵉʿāqāh* is the cry of the wronged that reaches YHWH — the *ṣᵉʿāqāh/zᵉʿāqāh* of Sodom (Gen 18:20–21) and of Israel in Egypt (Exod 3:7, 9), and the blood that “cries out” (*ṣōʿăqîm*) from the ground (Gen 4:10). It is rendered “an outcry” under the central `zaaqah-outcry-of-the-oppressed` entry, over ASV's flatter “a cry.”

paragraphs.translit: kī kerem YHWH ṣəbāʾōt bēt yiśrāʾēl wəʾīš yəhūdāh nəṭaʿ šaʿăšūʿāyw wayqaw ləmišpāṭ wəhinnēh miśpāḥ liṣdāqāh wəhinnēh ṣəʿāqāh (s)

paragraphs.text: ה֗וֹי מַגִּיעֵ֥י בַ֙יִת֙ בְּבַ֔יִת שָׂדֶ֥ה בְשָׂדֶ֖ה יַקְרִ֑יבוּ עַ֚ד אֶ֣פֶס מָק֔וֹם וְהֽוּשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם לְבַדְּכֶ֖ם בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: Woe to those who join house to house, who add field to field, until there is no room left, and you are made to dwell alone in the midst of the land!

notes.official: *hôy* opens the first of six woe-sayings (vv 8, 11, 18, 20, 21, 22), rendered “Woe” throughout. *ʾereṣ* here is the land of Israel, whose fields are being absorbed into great estates, and is rendered “land” (central `eretz`); contrast “the end of the earth” in v 26.

paragraphs.translit: hōy maggīʿē bayit bəbayit śādeh bəśādeh yaqrībū ʿad ʾepes māqōm wəhūšabtem ləbaddəkem bəqereb hāʾāreṣ

paragraphs.text: בְּאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם־לֹ֞א בָּתִּ֤ים רַבִּים֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה יִֽהְי֔וּ גְּדֹלִ֥ים וְטוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

i18n.en: In my ears YHWH of hosts says: Surely many houses shall become a desolation, great and fair ones, without inhabitant.

notes.official: *bᵉʾoznāy YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* has no verb: “in my ears, YHWH of hosts.” The translation supplies “says” with ASV; the oath particle *ʾim-lōʾ* “surely” that follows has suggested “has sworn in my hearing” (NRSV), and 22:14 gives the fuller form (“YHWH of hosts revealed himself in my ears”).

paragraphs.translit: bəʾoznāy YHWH ṣəbāʾōt ʾim-lōʾ bāttīm rabbīm ləšammāh yihyū gədōlīm wəṭōbīm mēʾēn yōšēb

paragraphs.text: כִּ֗י עֲשֶׂ֙רֶת֙ צִמְדֵּי־כֶ֔רֶם יַעֲשׂ֖וּ בַּ֣ת אֶחָ֑ת וְזֶ֥רַע חֹ֖מֶר יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֵיפָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: For ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield an ephah.

notes.official: *ṣimdê-ḵerem* are “yokes” of vineyard, the area a yoke of oxen ploughs in a day (ASV “acres”). A *bath* is a liquid measure and a *homer* is ten *ephahs* (Ezek 45:11), so the sown field returns a tenth of its seed.

paragraphs.translit: kī ʿăśeret ṣimdē-kerem yaʿăśū bat ʾeḥāt wəzeraʿ ḥōmer yaʿăśeh ʾēpāh (p)

paragraphs.text: ה֛וֹי מַשְׁכִּימֵ֥י בַבֹּ֖קֶר שֵׁכָ֣ר יִרְדֹּ֑פוּ מְאַחֲרֵ֣י בַנֶּ֔שֶׁף יַ֖יִן יַדְלִיקֵֽם׃

i18n.en: Woe to those who rise early in the morning to pursue strong drink, who linger late into the evening until wine inflames them!

paragraphs.translit: hōy maškīmē babbōqer šēkār yirdōpū məʾaḥărē bannešep yayin yadlīqēm

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֨ה כִנּ֜וֹר וָנֶ֗בֶל תֹּ֧ף וְחָלִ֛יל וָיַ֖יִן מִשְׁתֵּיהֶ֑ם וְאֵ֨ת פֹּ֤עַל יְהוָה֙ לֹ֣א יַבִּ֔יטוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדָ֖יו לֹ֥א רָאֽוּ׃

i18n.en: And lyre and harp, timbrel and flute, and wine are at their feasts; but they do not regard the deed of YHWH, nor have they seen the work of his hands.

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh kinnōr wānebel tōp wəḥālīl wāyayin mištēhem wəʾēt pōʿal YHWH lōʾ yabbīṭū ūmaʿăśēh yādāyw lōʾ rāʾū

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֛ן גָּלָ֥ה עַמִּ֖י מִבְּלִי־דָ֑עַת וּכְבוֹדוֹ֙ מְתֵ֣י רָעָ֔ב וַהֲמוֹנ֖וֹ צִחֵ֥ה צָמָֽא׃

i18n.en: Therefore my people have gone into exile for lack of knowledge; and their honored men are famished, and their multitude is parched with thirst.

notes.official: *gālāh ʿammî* is a perfect, “my people have gone into exile”; it may also be read as a prophetic perfect (“shall go”), and the line keeps the past form. In *ūḵᵉḇôḏô mᵉṯê rāʿāḇ*, *kāḇôḏ* is the people's “glory” in the social sense, its nobility, set against *hămônô* “its multitude.” The singular suffixes refer to the collective *ʿammî* “my people” and are rendered “their” (ASV, JPS 1917). The divine *kāḇôḏ* entry does not apply. MT *mᵉṯê* “men of (hunger)” is kept, giving “their honored men are famished”; the Septuagint's *nekrōn* “dead” supports the repointing *mēṯê* “dying of hunger” (NRSV), reported here and not adopted (`mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: lākēn gālāh ʿammī mibbəlī-dāʿat ūkəbōdō mətē rāʿāb wahămōnō ṣiḥēh ṣāmāʾ

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֗ן הִרְחִ֤יבָה שְּׁאוֹל֙ נַפְשָׁ֔הּ וּפָעֲרָ֥ה פִ֖יהָ לִבְלִי־חֹ֑ק וְיָרַ֨ד הֲדָרָ֧הּ וַהֲמוֹנָ֛הּ וּשְׁאוֹנָ֖הּ וְעָלֵ֥ז בָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: Therefore She'ol has widened its throat and opened its mouth beyond measure; and down go her splendor and her multitude, her uproar and the one who exults in her.

notes.official:
*hirḥîḇāh šᵉʾôl nap̄šāh* uses *nep̄eš* in its physical sense, “throat, gullet” (HALOT; NJPS “gullet”), parallel to *pîhā* “its mouth.” The translation renders “has widened its throat” over ASV's “enlarged its desire”; the same idiom describes greed at Hab 2:5 (“who widens his *nep̄eš* like She'ol”). The image of Death as a gaping maw has a Ugaritic parallel in Mot's swallowing jaws (KTU 1.5 II 2–4).

The feminine suffixes in *hăḏārāh wahămônāh ūšᵉʾônāh … bāh* (“her splendor … in her”) refer to a feminine noun the verse does not name, most likely Jerusalem (v 3). ASV and JPS 1917 both smooth them to “their … among them”; the translation keeps “her,” with NRSV, which names the referent (“the nobility of Jerusalem and her multitude … all who exult in her”).

paragraphs.translit: lākēn hirḥībāh šəʾōl napšāh ūpāʿărāh pīhā liblī-ḥōq wəyārad hădārāh wahămōnāh ūšəʾōnāh wəʿālēz bāh

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ח אָדָ֖ם וַיִּשְׁפַּל־אִ֑ישׁ וְעֵינֵ֥י גְבֹהִ֖ים תִּשְׁפַּֽלְנָה׃

i18n.en: And humankind is bowed down, and everyone is brought low, and the eyes of the lofty are brought low.

notes.official: *wayyiššaḥ ʾāḏām wayyišpal-ʾîš* repeats 2:9 (cf. 2:11, 17), and the line renders it as there, “humankind is bowed down, and everyone is brought low.” The two nouns are read as synonyms (JPS 1917 “man … man”; NRSV “people … everyone”), and *ʾîš* is “everyone” so that the pair is not split between a neutral and a gendered English word (overlay `adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah`). ASV's “the mean man … the great man” reads a social merism the text does not mark; it is recorded here as the main alternative.

paragraphs.translit: wayyiššaḥ ʾādām wayyišpal-ʾīš wəʿēnē gəbōhīm tišpalnāh

paragraphs.text: וַיִּגְבַּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וְהָאֵל֙ הַקָּד֔וֹשׁ נִקְדָּ֖שׁ בִּצְדָקָֽה׃

i18n.en: But YHWH of hosts is exalted in justice, and God the Holy One is sanctified in righteousness.

notes.official: *hāʾēl haqqāḏôš niqdaš biṣḏāqāh*: the articular phrase may be appositional, “God, the Holy One” (ASV, JPS 1917), or attributive, “the holy God” (NRSV, NJPS); the line keeps ASV. The Niphal *niqdaš* is “is sanctified” in the sense of “shows himself holy” — YHWH's holiness made visible by acts of judgment (cf. Ezek 28:22). *mišpāṭ* and *ṣᵉḏāqāh* return from v 7 and are rendered as there; as at 32:16, the split pair is not placed under the central justice-pair entry.

paragraphs.translit: wayyigbah YHWH ṣəbāʾōt bammišpāṭ wəhāʾēl haqqādōš niqdāš biṣdāqāh

paragraphs.text: וְרָע֥וּ כְבָשִׂ֖ים כְּדָבְרָ֑ם וְחָרְב֥וֹת מֵחִ֖ים גָּרִ֥ים יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

i18n.en: Then lambs shall graze as in their pasture, and sojourners shall eat the ruins of the fat ones.

notes.official: *wᵉḥārᵉḇôṯ mēḥîm gārîm yōʾḵēlû*: MT reads *gārîm* “sojourners” (ASV “wanderers”), rendered here as *gēr* is at 14:1, with *mēḥîm* “fat ones” (fatlings, or the wealthy owners). The Septuagint has *arnes* “lambs,” behind the conjectures *kārîm* “lambs” and *gᵉḏāyîm* “kids” (NRSV “fatlings and kids shall feed among the ruins”). The line keeps MT under `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`.

paragraphs.translit: wərāʿū kəbāśīm kədābərām wəḥārəbōt mēḥīm gārīm yōʾkēlū

paragraphs.text: ה֛וֹי מֹשְׁכֵ֥י הֶֽעָוֺ֖ן בְּחַבְלֵ֣י הַשָּׁ֑וְא וְכַעֲב֥וֹת הָעֲגָלָ֖ה חַטָּאָֽה׃

i18n.en: Woe to those who drag iniquity with cords of falsehood, and sin as with cart ropes,

paragraphs.translit: hōy mōšəkē heʿāwn bəḥablē haššāwəʾ wəkaʿăbōt hāʿăgālāh ḥaṭṭāʾāh

paragraphs.text: הָאֹמְרִ֗ים יְמַהֵ֧ר ׀ יָחִ֛ישָׁה מַעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ לְמַ֣עַן נִרְאֶ֑ה וְתִקְרַ֣ב וְתָב֗וֹאָה עֲצַ֛ת קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְנֵדָֽעָה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: who say: “Let him make haste, let him hasten his work, that we may see it; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it!”

paragraphs.translit: hāʾōmərīm yəmahēr | yāḥīšāh maʿăśēhū ləmaʿan nirʾeh wətiqrab wətābōʾāh ʿăṣat qədōš yiśrāʾēl wənēdāʿāh (s)

paragraphs.text: ה֣וֹי הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לָרַ֛ע ט֖וֹב וְלַטּ֣וֹב רָ֑ע שָׂמִ֨ים חֹ֤שֶׁךְ לְאוֹר֙ וְא֣וֹר לְחֹ֔שֶׁךְ שָׂמִ֥ים מַ֛ר לְמָת֖וֹק וּמָת֥וֹק לְמָֽר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter!

paragraphs.translit: hōy hāʾōmərīm lāraʿ ṭōb wəlaṭṭōb rāʿ śāmīm ḥōšek ləʾōr wəʾōr ləḥōšek śāmīm mar ləmātōq ūmātōq ləmār (s)

paragraphs.text: ה֖וֹי חֲכָמִ֣ים בְּעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְנֶ֥גֶד פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם נְבֹנִֽים׃

i18n.en: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and discerning in their own sight!

paragraphs.translit: hōy ḥăkāmīm bəʿēnēhem wəneged pənēhem nəbōnīm

paragraphs.text: ה֕וֹי גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים לִשְׁתּ֣וֹת יָ֑יִן וְאַנְשֵׁי־חַ֖יִל לִמְסֹ֥ךְ שֵׁכָֽר׃

i18n.en: Woe to those who are mighty at drinking wine, and valiant men at mixing strong drink,

paragraphs.translit: hōy gibbōrīm lištōt yāyin wəʾanšē-ḥayil limsōk šēkār

paragraphs.text: מַצְדִּיקֵ֥י רָשָׁ֖ע עֵ֣קֶב שֹׁ֑חַד וְצִדְקַ֥ת צַדִּיקִ֖ים יָסִ֥ירוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: who acquit the wicked for a bribe, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!

paragraphs.translit: maṣdīqē rāšāʿ ʿēqeb šōḥad wəṣidqat ṣaddīqīm yāsīrū mimmennū (s)

paragraphs.text: לָכֵן֩ כֶּאֱכֹ֨ל קַ֜שׁ לְשׁ֣וֹן אֵ֗שׁ וַחֲשַׁ֤שׁ לֶֽהָבָה֙ יִרְפֶּ֔ה שָׁרְשָׁם֙ כַּמָּ֣ק יִֽהְיֶ֔ה וּפִרְחָ֖ם כָּאָבָ֣ק יַעֲלֶ֑ה כִּ֣י מָאֲס֗וּ אֵ֚ת תּוֹרַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְאֵ֛ת אִמְרַ֥ת קְדֽוֹשׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִאֵֽצוּ׃

i18n.en: Therefore, as the tongue of fire devours the stubble, and as dry grass sinks down in the flame, so their root shall be like rottenness, and their blossom shall go up like dust; for they have rejected the teaching of YHWH of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

notes.official: *tôraṯ YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* is rendered “the teaching of YHWH of hosts” (overlay `torah-teaching-isaiah`), parallel to *ʾimraṯ qᵉḏôš-yiśrāʾēl* “the word of the Holy One of Israel”: prophetic instruction rather than a law-code, as at 1:10.

paragraphs.translit: lākēn keʾĕkōl qaš ləšōn ʾēš waḥăšaš lehābāh yirpeh šoršām kammāq yihyeh ūpirḥām kāʾābāq yaʿăleh kī māʾăsū ʾēt tōrat YHWH ṣəbāʾōt wəʾēt ʾimrat qədōš-yiśrāʾēl niʾēṣū

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֡ן חָרָה֩ אַף־יְהוָ֨ה בְּעַמּ֜וֹ וַיֵּ֣ט יָד֧וֹ עָלָ֣יו וַיַּכֵּ֗הוּ וַֽיִּרְגְּזוּ֙ הֶֽהָרִ֔ים וַתְּהִ֧י נִבְלָתָ֛ם כַּסּוּחָ֖ה בְּקֶ֣רֶב חוּצ֑וֹת בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃

i18n.en: Therefore the anger of YHWH has been kindled against his people, and he has stretched out his hand against them and struck them, and the mountains quaked, and their corpses were like refuse in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger has not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.

notes.official:
The verse closes with the refrain *bᵉḵol-zōʾṯ lōʾ-šāḇ ʾappô wᵉʿôḏ yāḏô nᵉṭûyāh*, which returns four times in the poem of 9:7–10:4 (Heb. 9:11, 16, 20; 10:4). Its wording is fixed here so that it can carry through those chapters: “For all this his anger has not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.” *šûḇ ʾap* is the idiom for anger subsiding (Gen 27:44–45), so “turned away” (ASV, NRSV) is kept rather than the literal “turned back.” Many commentators hold that 5:25–30 has been displaced from that poem (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 1–39*, AB 19, 2000; Williamson).

The perfects and narrative verbs are rendered as past (“has been kindled … struck … quaked”). The blow has already fallen and the refrain says it is not the last.

paragraphs.translit: ʿal-kēn ḥārāh ʾap-YHWH bəʿammō wayyēṭ yādō ʿālāyw wayyakkēhū wayyirgəzū hehārīm wattəhī niblātām kassūḥāh bəqereb ḥūṣōt bəkol-zōʾt lōʾ-šāb ʾappō wəʿōd yādō nəṭūyāh

paragraphs.text: וְנָֽשָׂא־נֵ֤ס לַגּוֹיִם֙ מֵרָח֔וֹק וְשָׁ֥רַק ל֖וֹ מִקְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֥ה מְהֵרָ֖ה קַ֥ל יָבֽוֹא׃

i18n.en: And he will raise a signal for the nations from afar, and whistle for them from the end of the earth; and behold, they shall come with speed, swiftly.

notes.official: After *laggôyim mērāḥôq* “for the nations from afar,” every pronoun and verb through v 30 is singular (*lô* “for it,” *yāḇôʾ* “it comes”), picturing one army. Many emend to *lᵉḡôy mimmerḥāq* “for a nation from afar” (cf. Jer 5:15; NRSV). The translation keeps MT “nations” and, with ASV and JPS 1917, renders the singulars as collective “them / they.” *miqqᵉṣēh hāʾāreṣ* is the horizon idiom, “from the end of the earth” (overlay `eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24`).

paragraphs.translit: wənāśāʾ-nēs laggōyim mērāḥōq wəšāraq lō miqṣēh hāʾāreṣ wəhinnēh məhērāh qal yābōʾ

paragraphs.text: אֵין־עָיֵ֤ף וְאֵין־כּוֹשֵׁל֙ בּ֔וֹ לֹ֥א יָנ֖וּם וְלֹ֣א יִישָׁ֑ן וְלֹ֤א נִפְתַּח֙ אֵז֣וֹר חֲלָצָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א נִתַּ֖ק שְׂר֥וֹךְ נְעָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: None is weary and none stumbles among them; none slumbers nor sleeps; the belt of their loins is not loosed, nor the thong of their sandals broken;

paragraphs.translit: ʾēn-ʿāyēp wəʾēn-kōšēl bō lōʾ yānūm wəlōʾ yīšān wəlōʾ niptaḥ ʾēzōr ḥălāṣāyw wəlōʾ nittaq śərōk nəʿālāyw

paragraphs.text: אֲשֶׁ֤ר חִצָּיו֙ שְׁנוּנִ֔ים וְכָל־קַשְּׁתֹתָ֖יו דְּרֻכ֑וֹת פַּרְס֤וֹת סוּסָיו֙ כַּצַּ֣ר נֶחְשָׁ֔בוּ וְגַלְגִּלָּ֖יו כַּסּוּפָֽה׃

i18n.en: their arrows are sharp, and all their bows are bent; the hoofs of their horses are counted as flint, and their wheels as the whirlwind.

paragraphs.translit: ʾăšer ḥiṣṣāyw šənūnīm wəkol-qaššətōtāyw dərukōt parsōt sūsāyw kaṣṣar neḥšābū wəgalgillāyw kassūpāh

paragraphs.text: שְׁאָגָ֥ה ל֖וֹ כַּלָּבִ֑יא ושאג [יִשְׁאַ֨ג] כַּכְּפִירִ֤ים וְיִנְהֹם֙ וְיֹאחֵ֣ז טֶ֔רֶף וְיַפְלִ֖יט וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּֽיל׃

i18n.en: Their roaring is like a lioness; they roar like young lions; they growl and seize the prey, and carry it off, and there is none to deliver.

notes.official: Ketiv *wᵉšāʾaḡ* “and it roars,” qere *yišʾaḡ* “it roars”: the same verb and sense, differing only in form. The line translates the qere (`mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`); the source text keeps the ketiv with the qere in brackets.

paragraphs.translit: šəʾāgāh lō kallābīʾ wšʾg [yišʾag] kakkəpīrīm wəyinhōm wəyōʾḥēz ṭerep wəyaplīṭ wəʾēn maṣṣīl

paragraphs.text: וְיִנְהֹ֥ם עָלָ֛יו בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כְּנַהֲמַת־יָ֑ם וְנִבַּ֤ט לָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וְהִנֵּה־חֹ֔שֶׁךְ צַ֣ר וָא֔וֹר חָשַׁ֖ךְ בַּעֲרִיפֶֽיהָ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And they shall growl over it in that day like the growling of the sea; and if one looks to the land, behold, darkness and distress, and the light is darkened in its clouds.

notes.official: The accents divide the second half as “behold, darkness; distress and light; darkened in its clouds.” The translation follows ASV's grouping, “darkness and distress, and the light is darkened in its clouds.” *ʿărîp̄îm* is a hapax, “clouds” (cf. *ʿărāp̄el* “thick darkness”). *ṣar* “distress” is a homonym of the *ṣar* “flint” of v 28. *ʾereṣ* is “the land” (central `eretz`), the ground the invader overruns.

paragraphs.translit: wəyinhōm ʿālāyw bayyōm hahūʾ kənahămat-yām wənibbaṭ lāʾāreṣ wəhinnēh-ḥōšek ṣar wāʾōr ḥāšak baʿărīpēhā (p)
